channel.title: Research Tape
channel.description: A daily AI-in-finance research tape: arXiv and SSRN, six items or fewer.

item.title: Do LLM Valuation Agents Read the Filing? Metamorphic Tests of Filing Fidelity on Korean Listed Firms
item.description: Even with arithmetic delegated to Python, none of four preregistered primary hypotheses survives Holm correction across 150 Korean firms.

item.title: Look-ahead index membership and the relative accuracy of stock forecast
item.description: Look-ahead index rosters bias forecast comparisons against ML models, shrinking the Nasdaq-100 ML advantage over small size by about 90%.

item.title: OOM-RL II: Reality Is an Oracle, Not a Debugger Provenance-Constrained Diagnosis in Continually Evolving Agent-Engineered Systems
item.description: External outcome feedback can constrain claims about a trading system's returns but cannot identify which evolving procedure produced them without provenance binding.

item.title: Agents Propose, Code Decides: An Autonomous Research Loop Framework to Build an Equity Alpha Model
item.description: Agent-proposed predictors held their rank IC out of sample, but the hedged long-short retained only about half its expected Sharpe.

item.title: Agent Policy-Value Audit: Separating Transition Composition from Event Selection in Financial LLM Agents
item.description: The agent's +15.2 bps/event gross deployment value is explained by transition composition, leaving selection value at -10.6 bps and no detectable skill.

item.title: Noisy Financial Machine Learning
item.description: Against the panel historical mean rather than the zero forecast, only flexible nonlinear models show consistent gains, concentrated in small, value and illiquid stocks.

item.title: Large Language Models and Information Frictions in Corporate Bonds
item.description: LLM-read earnings calls forecast rating migration a year ahead, and bond returns only where analysts disagreed, while post-earnings drift is not explained by it.

item.title: MintEval: Do LLMs Implement the Trading Strategy You Asked For? A Behavioural-Equivalence Benchmark for Natural-Language-to-Strategy Code
item.description: A frontier model silently diverges from the requested strategy on 27.5% of tasks, and a recent LLM-judge benchmark accepts every such failure.

item.title: Mixture-of-Experts for Cryptocurrency Order Execution: Training Stability, Tail Risk, and Failure Modes
item.description: Annealed exploration alone eliminates policy collapse in this environment, making expert partitioning unnecessary, and within-policy tail risk rises monotonically with K.

item.title: Silent Implementation Shortfall in LLM-Written Trading Code
item.description: Frontier LLMs silently diverge from trading strategy intent on over a quarter of tasks.

item.title: Artifact Integrity Does Not Imply Temporal Integrity: Evaluating Evidence-Bound Gates for Financial Research Agents
item.description: Financial artifacts with verified byte integrity can still contain temporally invalid information.

item.title: LLM Pricing Agents as Rote Learners
item.description: Increased prompt context makes LLM pricing agents more consistent without making them more accurate.

item.title: Common AI Information and Capital Allocation
item.description: AI progress expands investor information but reduces price informativeness for firms, worsening capital allocation.

item.title: Calibrated Gating in Financial RAG: Small External Controllers versus LLM Self-Assessment across Model Scales
item.description: A 0.3B calibrated model beats LLM self-assessment for financial RAG evidence-sufficiency gating.

item.title: LLM-Driven Sentiment Shocks and Nonlinear Contagion in Global Banking Networks: A Hybrid SEM–ANN–GARCH Approach
item.description: LLM sentiment shocks correlate positively with financial contagion in banking networks.

item.title: Do Your Own Research: Learning to Forecast by Learning to Search
item.description: Outcome-based training teaches agents evidence discipline, reducing searches while improving forecast calibration.

item.title: Large Language Models, Debt Renegotiation, and Contract Enforcement
item.description: LLM-written messages outperform human-written messages in distressed-debt renegotiation.

item.title: LiveOption: Evaluating LLM Agents in Structured Option Trading with Nonlinear Payoffs
item.description: LLM agents underperform on structured option trading with nonlinear payoffs.

item.title: EverMine: Dissecting the Self-Evolution of Research Capabilities in Long-Horizon Alpha Research
item.description: Capability evolution provides no consistent gains in alpha discovery.

item.title: RICE-Alpha: Reliability-Informed Correction with Event Graphs for LLM-Agent Stock Forecasting
item.description: Historical event continuation adds forecast value when temporally grounded and reliability-calibrated.

item.title: From Search to Research: Exploring Search Scaling in Autonomous Quantitative Factor Mining
item.description: Model capability matters more than search depth in initial autonomous research.

item.title: An Integrated Framework of Financial Feature States, Scenario Candidates and a Lightweight Local Selection Model: A Matched-Information Comparison for S&P 500 Price-Path Selection
item.description: Lightweight language models underperform conventional baselines for S&P 500 price-path selection despite financial adaptation.

item.title: Do Narratives Lead Prices, Or Follow Them? Sentiment, Price Positioning, And Measurement Disagreement In Bitcoin
item.description: Bitcoin prices predict sentiment, reversing the leading-indicator interpretation of published sentiment indices.

item.title: Epistemic Calibration and Latency Advantages of System One Probabilistic Agents in Limit Order Book Microstructure: An Empirical and Multi-Agent Evaluation
item.description: Autoregressive LLMs encounter prohibitive latencies (3.5–12 seconds) when deployed in electronic financial markets.

item.title: Silicon Cartels: Detector Orientation in Multi-Agent Pricing Testbeds
item.description: Testbed detector calibration against low-variance controls reverses polarity in higher-variance deployment environments.

item.title: Agentic Regulatory Intelligence: A Human-Supervised Multi-Agent System Architecture for Financial Crime Pattern Monitoring and Regulatory Guidance Generation
item.description: Regulatory guidance for financial crimes lags 12–57 months after typology emergence, extending criminal opportunities.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence, Model Monoculture, and Bank Credit Allocation
item.description: AI development increases convergence in bank credit allocation, reducing system-wide lending diversity.

item.title: What the Fed Hears and What It Concludes: Supply-Chain Narratives and U.S. Inflation Forecasting ⋆
item.description: FOMC narratives improve inflation forecast accuracy while Beige Book narratives do not.

item.title: Order Invariance at the Last Language-Model Boundary: A Pre-Registered Test of an LLM Evidence Synthesizer Inside a Deterministic Trading Architecture
item.description: Language model nondeterminism, not input order sensitivity, drives trading system uncertainty.

item.title: When Stress Tests Miss the Risk: Statistical Scenario Analysis for Financial Portfolios
item.description: Standard scenario analysis substantially understates portfolio risk by overlooking factor dependence.

item.title: Adaptive State Representation and Critical Explainability Evaluation for A2C-Based Algorithmic Carbon Allowance Trading
item.description: A2C trading agent performance is sensitive to random initialization despite high reported Sharpe ratios.

item.title: Abstention Is Not Neutral: Ablating the LLM in an LLM Trading Agent
item.description: Language model trading agent abstention is primarily determined by prompt wording, not market conditions.

item.title: Residual Learning in Empirical Asset Pricing
item.description: Deep neural networks outperform shallow models in asset pricing when trained with residual learning.

item.title: Propose, Don't Judge: An Anytime-Valid Referee for LLM Agents That Mine Investment Factors
item.description: Frozen referees outperform leaky referees at controlling spurious factors.

item.title: The Price of Thought: Does Test-Time Reasoning Pay in LLM Trading?
item.description: LLM test-time reasoning changes trading decisions without reliably improving returns.

item.title: What Analysts Miss: Predicting Consensus Forecast Errors from Earnings Calls
item.description: Analyst forecast errors are predictable from earnings-call language and profitable to trade around announcements.

item.title: The Externality of Learning: Adaptive AI and Market Resilience
item.description: Shared learning histories improve market resilience when policies are learned via locality-sensitive algorithms.

item.title: An Auditable Public-Data U.S. Equity Research Pipeline: Point-in-Time Factors, Asset Pricing, Portfolio Construction, and Walk-Forward Machine Learning
item.description: Higher R-squared in multifactor models doesn't translate to stable after-cost portfolio outperformance.

item.title: DefaultGNN: A Dual-Perspective GNN Framework for Predicting Corporate Default from Buyer-Seller Transaction Networks
item.description: Buyer-seller transaction networks predict default better than financial data for information-sparse firms.

item.title: When the Market Moves but the Model Does Not: Stale Financial Information in LLMs
item.description: LLMs generate persistent trading losses when forecasting beyond their training data without current price information.

item.title: The Anonymity Paradox: Identity Disclosure, Online Information Production, and Stock Price Efficiency
item.description: Real-name policies reduce stock price informativeness by suppressing retail information production on social platforms.

item.title: Planning External-Data Adoption in Energy-Market Forecasting: A Matched Decision Framework for Global News
item.description: Best energy forecasts use market data alone, not augmented with external news.

item.title: Forecasting, Forward Contracting, and Retailer Performance in a Regulated Electricity Market
item.description: Better spot-price forecasts only improve electricity trading profits if retailers can flexibly adjust forward positions.

item.title: Systematic Alpha Discovery in Foreign Exchange Markets A Two-phase Research Program: From Exhaustive Structural-factor Search to Fundamentals-Driven Machine Learning
item.description: Exhaustive FX factor searches identify zero exploitable edges under statistical validation.

item.title: Asymmetric Volatility Transmission Between AI Compute Infrastructure and Regional Power Grids: Evidence from Quantile Connectedness Under Extreme Market States
item.description: Volatility transmission between AI infrastructure and power grids reverses during crises.

item.title: Label alchemy: Target engineering for improved stock selection
item.description: Label choice drives larger stock-selection performance variation than model or feature selection.

item.title: Prices or implied volatilities? Choosing the loss function in machine learning option pricing
item.description: Training option-pricing models on price errors beats implied-volatility loss by 25%.

item.title: Agentic AI as a Lens on Human Decision Making: Field Experimental Evidence from Dynamic Pricing
item.description: AI pricing advantage exploits incumbent conventions, suggesting performance gains are transient.

item.title: Inflation narratives and risk premia
item.description: Demand-minus-supply narratives predict inflation risk premia better than PMI or forecasters.

item.title: LLM-Based Semantic Surprises in FOMC Communication: Asset Prices and Financial-Market Stress
item.description: Fed semantic novelty increases financial stress only in high-stress market regimes.

item.title: Welcome to the Factor Zoo: Where Mutual Fund Alpha Hides
item.description: LASSO benchmarks reveal active mutual fund alpha Fama-French models obscure.

item.title: Beta Recall, Alpha Recall, and a Contamination Detector that Needs No Labels * Measuring Training-data Leakage in LLM Equity Signals
item.description: LLM stock-ranking performance inside its training window is substantially recall-based rather than predictive.

item.title: Execution-Aware Alpha Mining: Teaching LLM Factor Agents to Account for Trading Costs​
item.description: LLM alpha-mining agents optimized on gross returns converge to economically catastrophic turnover without explicit execution-cost penalties.

item.title: SoK: Trading Agents or Market Crashers? Dissecting Robustness and Security Failures in Academic Financial LLM Trading Schemes
item.description: Every academic LLM trading agent scheme examined exhibits security vulnerabilities enabling low-cost market-crash attacks.

item.title: Why Discovery Layers Guarantee Crowded Alpha: A Design Case for Quality-Diversity Search in Agentic Trading Systems
item.description: A discovery layer optimized purely for predictive quality is structurally guaranteed to converge on crowded factors.

item.title: A Three-Layer Reference Architecture for Deterministic Control in Agentic Trading Systems
item.description: Three-layer architectures with hard-gated execution prevent documented agentic trading failures.

item.title: EvolveTrade: Experience-Driven Policy Refinement for Self-Evolving LLM Trading Agents
item.description: System-prompt evolution using portfolio feedback improves LLM trading agents' Sharpe ratios in tested market regimes.

item.title: A Causality-Gated Multi-Agent System for Generative Feature Engineering in Financial Markets
item.description: Information leakage explains the apparent edge in LLM-generated financial features.

item.title: Do a Legislator's Trades Anticipate Legislative Acts? Timing, Disclosure and Proximity Tests on the STOCK Act Filings of the Pelosi Household, 2014–2026
item.description: Pelosi's trades fail timing, disclosure, and proximity tests for legislative anticipation.

item.title: From Backtest to Deployment: A Staged-capital Protocol for Evaluating Agentic Trading Systems - A Position Paper Proposing an Engineering Workflow for Committing Real Capital to Autonomous Trading Agents
item.description: Mechanical exit rules outperform discretionary logic in live agentic trading systems.

item.title: From Hindsight to Foresight: Adapting Reusable Reasoning Structures from Recurring Financial Events
item.description: Reusing reasoning paths from past recurring events improves LLM financial forecasts.

item.title: Fedspeak, LLM-Derived Signals, and High-Frequency Trading
item.description: Fed communication divergence generates systematic intraday price movements and position reallocation.

item.title: Automated Alpha Discovery Under Rigorous Out-of-Sample Validation: A Forensic Study of Trading Signal Search
item.description: No trading signals from automated price/volume search survive rigorous out-of-sample validation.

item.title: Moral Inflation in Synthetic Investors: When LLM Personas Replace Heterogeneity with Normative Archetypes
item.description: LLM-based synthetic investors suppress heterogeneity and amplify moral effects.

item.title: FinRL-DeepSeek Revisited: A Reproduction and Multi-Seed Robustness Analysis of LLM-Infused Risk-Sensitive Trading Agents
item.description: Single-seed financial backtests undermine published agent rankings by obscuring seed-dependent performance reversals.

item.title: FinProof v1: An Adversarial Benchmark for AI Guardrail Evaluation in Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance
item.description: Generic AI safety benchmarks systematically miss BFSI-specific attacks exploiting regulatory complexity and compliance ambiguity.

item.title: The Operating-Layer Dominance Hypothesis: Why Agentic Trading Alpha Is an Interface Problem, Not a Model Problem A Position Paper on Architecture, Live Evaluation, and Alpha Limits in Multi-Agent Trading Systems
item.description: Deterministic execution-layer control, not model capability, is the binding constraint on agentic trading alpha.

item.title: Named Entity Recognition for Unstructured Financial Transaction Text
item.description: Span-matching architectures disambiguate financial transaction boundaries more efficiently than transformers under limited labeled data.

item.title: How Much is Too Much Optimism? Peer Tone Benchmarking and the Market Discount for Positive Tone Deviation
item.description: Unverified peer-relative optimism in MD&A triggers a 2-4% market-to-book valuation penalty.

item.title: Can Machines Learn Electricity Hedging Regimes? State-Dependent Minimum-Variance Hedging in German Power Futures
item.description: State-dependent hedging using neural network regime-weighting reduces power-futures tail risk by 10 EUR/MWh versus OLS.

item.title: When Does LLM-Extracted Central Bank Sentiment Add Value? A Fragility Analysis of Sentiment-Tilted CVaR Portfolios in FX Markets
item.description: LLM-extracted sentiment from central bank statements fails to provide statistically significant portfolio improvements.

item.title: Do Capital-Goods Incentive Announcements Move Italian Industrial Stocks? An Event Study with LLM-Coded Regulatory Acts, 2019–2026
item.description: Italian capital-goods incentive policies produce no measurable abnormal stock returns upon announcement.

item.title: Agentic Decision Mathematics: Risk-Constrained Allocation of Operational Autonomy Under Uncertainty in Financial Market Infrastructure
item.description: AI operational autonomy should be formalized as a constrained, optimizable resource managed through mathematics.

item.title: Computation Is Explanation: An Active Inference Agent for Interpretable Portfolio Control
item.description: Active Inference embeds portfolio control explanations in decision computation, enabling true ante-hoc interpretability.

item.title: Which Learned Forecaster Wins, and When? A Regime-and Horizon-Conditioned Comparison of Recurrent, Attentional, Generative and Tree-Based Stock-Forecasting Models, with a Regime-Switching Mixture of Experts
item.description: Regime-Switching Mixture of Experts beats individual forecasters without requiring ex-ante knowledge of which is best.

item.title: Delegated Consumption and the Missing Discipline of Competition An Equilibrium Theory of the AI Token Market
item.description: Delegated AI execution lets firms control unauditable consumption intensity, neutralizing token-price competition benefits.

item.title: The Friction Ledger: A Zero-Sum Accounting of Polymarket Order Flow and the Geometry of Event-Contract Fees
item.description: Prediction market taker fees consume 10.4 times the gross edge of active traders.

item.title: Large Language Models, Price Discovery, and Synchronized Trading
item.description: Frontier language models improve price discovery in hard-to-read firms despite synchronizing order flow.

item.title: Calibration that counts: Conformal prediction intervals for automated valuation models
item.description: Prediction intervals from hedonic, boosted, and neural-network AVMs fail calibration worst during interest-rate shocks.

item.title: Heterogeneity by Design for AI Liquidity Management Agents on Instant Payment Rails: A Conformance Specification
item.description: Shared models among autonomous liquidity agents create herding risk requiring conformance-tested institutional heterogeneity.

item.title: Trade-Policy and Export-Control Exposure, Validated Textual Disclosure, and Capital-Market Outcomes
item.description: Underdisclosed export-control exposure does not predict crash risk or illiquidity, despite material underlying exposure.

item.title: When Does Reinforcement Learning Beat Naive Diversification? Learning Architecture, Regime Information, and Trading Frictions
item.description: Decision Transformers substantially outperform both online actor-critic RL and equally-weighted portfolio benchmarks.

item.title: Quorum: A Benchmark for Financial Artificial Intelligence under Contested Ground Truth
item.description: Sovereigns crossing investment-grade boundaries face median two-year rating-agency disagreement.

item.title: Valu(AI)tion: Machine Value and Market Prices
item.description: Fundamental models generate 6.3% annual alpha despite algorithmic market dominance.

item.title: What Investors Believe and Why: Reasoning-Conditioned Sentiment in Cryptocurrency Markets
item.description: Conditioning Stocktwits sentiment on reasoning quality improves cryptocurrency return prediction.

item.title: Do Large Language Models Add Value in Credit Investing? Evidence from a Disclosure-Reading Agent for US Bank Bonds
item.description: Language models reading bank disclosures can identify credit deterioration before it affects bond prices.

item.title: A Pre-registered, Cryptographically Timestamped Proving Protocol for Directional Market Forecasting, with Announced Echo State Network and Quantum Reservoir Computing Examinations
item.description: Directional forecasting models underperform simple price-based forecasts even with careful pre-registration.

item.title: Does Empirical Finance Replicate?
item.description: Published finance studies replicate in-sample but collapse out-of-sample, consistent with data snooping.

item.title: Point-in-Time SEC Financial Data: A Reproducible Benchmark for Detecting Look-Ahead and Restatement Leakage
item.description: Financial data services leak look-ahead bias into historical backtests through retention rules.

item.title: A Thousand Agents, One Opinion: Effective Population Collapse in LLM-based Artificial Markets
item.description: Aligned language-model agents exhibit high cross-correlation, reducing sixteen agents to 2.6 effective traders.

item.title: Reasoning More, Knowing No Better? Epistemic Calibration in Financial Reasoning Tasks
item.description: Increased reasoning effort improves LLM accuracy on financial tasks without improving calibration.

item.title: When LLMs Whisper: Information Leakage and Collusion in Financial Markets
item.description: LLM reasoning traces could enable tacit collusion by revealing rivals' intended orders.

item.title: ChatGPT as Information Intermediary: Media Partnerships, Sycophancy, and the Pricing of Earnings News
item.description: Generative AI intermediaries distort earnings pricing by controlling information salience and presentation bias.

item.title: The Great Codification: GenAI and Intangible Capital
item.description: Agentic AI destroys firm value when it codifies intangible capital into portable knowledge.

item.title: Regulatory Semantic Drift: When Preference-based Correction Fails Silently, FINCAC40, a Sixteen-year AMF Corpus (2010-2026) for Evaluating the Temporal Robustness of LLMs in ESG Classification
item.description: Preference-optimization fine-tuning can collapse ESG regulatory classification undetected by standard training metrics.

item.title: Unknown Is Not Zero: Heat Stress, Data-Center Power-Demand Exposure, and Utility Volatility
item.description: Treating unknown data-center exposure as verified zero manufactures spurious interaction effects in regression.

item.title: Signal Correlation, IC, and PnL Dependence
item.description: Signal correlation and PnL correlation are mathematically non-identifiable without constraints on portfolio construction.

item.title: Adversarial Training for Tabular Credit Scoring: A Multi-Attack Robustness Evaluation in P2P Lending
item.description: Single-attack adversarial training overstates credit-model robustness because defenses transfer weakly across attack types.

item.title: What LLM Trading Agents Actually Do in Production: A Six-Month, Population-Scale Record from Two Fleets
item.description: Risk settings determine LLM trading behavior more than written strategy text does.

item.title: TieOutBench: A Runnable, Rubric-Gated Evaluation Suite for Financial Analysis and Post-Trade Operations
item.description: Frontier financial LLMs fail to identify unreconciled baskets or mismatched confirmations.

item.title: What the Window Does Not Contain: Auditing Provenance in a Document-Grounded Instability Benchmark
item.description: Adding missing evidence to documents does not substantially reduce LLM answer instability.

item.title: Filtering without recursion and some of its uses in financial economics
item.description: Nonlinear filtering recovers volatility signatures from high-frequency data that linear methods cannot unbias.

item.title: GraphFAS: A Distributed System for Automated Graph Feature Generation and Selection in Industrial Transaction Networks
item.description: Non-parametric graph features enable fraud model interpretability that end-to-end GNNs cannot achieve.

item.title: The Market already Knew: A Pre-registered Falsification of TimesFM-3 on the SPY Implied-volatility Surface
item.description: Market-implied volatility forecasts outperform TimesFM-3 at both one and five-day prediction horizons.

item.title: Do Language Models Know Who Fails? Look-Ahead Bias in LLM Credit-Risk Assessment
item.description: LLM credit prediction beats baselines only because models memorized bankruptcy outcomes in training data.

item.title: When Financial Fine-tuning Fails: A Three-Level Detectability Analysis of Numerical Hallucination in Domain-Adapted Language Models
item.description: Financial domain fine-tuning increases LLM hallucination from 5% to 98% despite numeracy supervision.

item.title: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
item.description: More capable LLM traders exhibit correlated behavior that concentrates rather than diversifies market risk.

item.title: Convex Modeling of Price Cross-Impact over Time
item.description: Models omitting cross-impact and transient decay systematically overestimate costs for relative-value trades.
